seoTitle: Monday.com Tutorial for Beginners: Boards, Tasks, and AI
metaDescription: A beginner's guide to Monday.com covering boards, tasks, statuses, and where Sidekick, Agents, and its other AI tools sit in the interface.
intro: Monday.com organizes work as boards: colorful, spreadsheet-like tables where every row is a task and every column is a piece of information about it, like who owns it or when it's due. For a beginner the learning curve is really just learning to read one board well, since templates, task detail panels, and status columns all work the same way across every board you'll ever create. This guide covers setting up and navigating a board, updating task status, and where Monday.com's AI tools, currently named Sidekick, Agents, and Vibe, sit alongside the manual workflow.

steps.heading: Read a board's structure
steps.body: A Monday.com board is a table split into named groups, colored bands like "Supplier A" or "Supplier B", with each row inside a group being one item, and each column holding a specific data type: text, a person, a date, a status label, or a number. The toolbar above the table carries the tools that act on the whole board: New item to add a row, Filter and Sort to narrow what's shown, Group by to reorganize, and on the right, entry points into the AI features covered later in this guide. Every group and column total rolls up automatically at the bottom of the table, sums, counts, and date ranges, so you get a running summary without building a separate report.

image.caption: A Financial Accounting board grouped by supplier, with status columns like Payment 1 and Payment 2 color-coded Paid or Not Paid.

steps.heading: Start a new board from a template
steps.body: Instead of building a board from a blank grid, the Template center (reachable from the + next to your workspace) lets you browse by category, Marketing, Sales & CRM, Software Development, HR, and more, and preview a template before committing. Selecting one, like Project Management, shows how many users have adopted it and offers Use template to drop a ready-made structure of groups, columns, and sample items straight into your workspace, which you then rename and refill with your own data.

image.caption: The Template center, browsing the Project Management template before adding it to a workspace with Use template.

steps.heading: Update status directly in the table
steps.body: The Status column is the fastest way to see where work stands, and it's editable inline: click a cell and a dropdown of colored labels appears, Done, Working on it, Stuck, Not Started, plus an Edit Labels option if the defaults don't match your workflow. Changing a task's status here updates every view and rollup that depends on it immediately, which is what keeps Monday.com's dashboards and progress bars accurate without any manual recalculation. Auto-assign labels is also available from the same dropdown for cycling defaults automatically as items move through stages.

image.caption: Changing a task's Status inline from a dropdown of colored labels: Done, Working on it, Stuck, and Not Started.

steps.heading: Open a task for detail and updates
steps.body: Clicking a task's name (instead of one of its column cells) opens its full item card, with tabs for Updates, Files, and Activity Log. Updates is a running comment thread scoped to that one task: post progress notes, @mention a teammate, attach a file or GIF, and everyone with access sees the same thread instead of it getting buried in chat. It starts empty on a new task ("No updates yet"), and this is generally where the day-to-day conversation about a piece of work happens, separate from the structured columns on the board.

image.caption: A task's Updates tab: a comment thread for that item, starting empty until someone posts progress or mentions a teammate.

steps.heading: Know where the AI tools live
steps.body: The feature this guide's title refers to as "Sidekick AI" is Monday.com's assistant, and as of 2026 the platform calls it simply Sidekick, not "monday AI". It isn't tucked into one menu: it's reachable account-wide from the left panel, at board level from a star icon in the toolbar, and at item level from a star icon next to any individual task. Alongside Sidekick sit two separate tools worth knowing apart from it: Agents, built to run ongoing or repetitive work inside a board on their own, and Vibe, a prompt-to-app builder for generating small custom tools instead of a chat assistant. Treat these as an accelerator once you already understand a board's groups, columns, and statuses, not a replacement for learning the basics first.

steps.heading: Move between multiple boards without losing context
steps.body: A real workspace, like the sample PMN workspace shown throughout this walkthrough, holds many boards at once: Financial Accounting, Daily Work Schedule, KPI Dashboard, Inventory Management, Budget Plan, all listed in the left sidebar and switchable with a single click. Related boards can also be nested under a parent folder (as seen with Project Management containing High Level and Projects sub-items), worth setting up early if you expect the workspace to grow past a handful of boards, since flat lists get hard to navigate quickly.

faq.question: Is "monday AI" still the right name for Monday.com's assistant?
faq.answer: No. Monday.com now calls its assistant Sidekick. It's reachable from the left panel account-wide, and from star icons at the board and individual item level.

faq.question: Are Monday.com's AI features available on every plan?
faq.answer: It varies by feature. Sidekick's free tier gives a limited number of messages per day on the Standard and Pro plans, with higher tiers purchasable on any plan; Agents and Vibe are positioned as available across plans, according to Monday.com's own 2026 documentation.

faq.question: Do I need technical skills to use Monday.com as a beginner?
faq.answer: No. Monday.com is a visual, drag-and-drop tool: building a board, adding items, and changing statuses all happen by clicking cells in a table, with no code required.

faq.question: What's the difference between a board's columns and its Updates tab?
faq.answer: Columns hold structured data (status, owner, due date) that rolls up into totals and views. The Updates tab, opened from an individual task, is an unstructured comment thread for discussing that specific item.

faq.question: Can I start from a template instead of building a board from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. The Template center offers ready-made boards by category, Project Management, Marketing, Sales & CRM, and more, that you can preview and drop into your workspace with Use template.

faq.question: How is Monday.com different from a basic to-do list app?
faq.answer: Monday.com supports multiple boards, color-coded statuses, automatic rollups, task-level comment threads, and built-in AI and automation tools, well beyond a flat list of to-dos.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025, when the assistant was still commonly called "monday AI" (reflected in this article's slug and title, which are left unchanged). Re-checked against Monday.com's own 2026 product documentation in September 2026, which shows the assistant renamed to Sidekick with three distinct entry points, and Agents and Vibe as separate, non-chat AI tools. The dedicated support.monday.com AI Agents article could not be fetched directly (it returned a 403), so the plan-availability details here are sourced from Monday.com's own blog instead of its help center.
